A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIRECTO study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–K are readable and matchable despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix H report original graph-generation experiments, architectural ablations, scalability studies, and conditional-generation results.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional component ablations, positional-encoding comparisons, and computational-resource measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed DFM framework, dual attention, FiLM/PNA modulation, gated updates, losses, and training/sampling algorithms are retained. DirLap appears as an additional encoding comparator; the expanded explanations and redrawn architecture do not establish a revised proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ER, ER-DAG, SBM, Price graphs, TPU Tiles, and Visual Genome, including the existing graph-size and conditional-generation scenarios. The new ablations use retained datasets. Link prediction and node classification are suggested future applications, not evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Table 14 adds DirLap to the ER-DAG and SBM encoding comparisons, and new Table 16 adds component-removal comparators. Table 8 extends resource comparisons to existing benchmark baselines and DIRECTO-DD variants. The main benchmark comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 7 changes the reported optimal SBM/MagLap stochasticity parameter eta from 10 to 50, without establishing that experiments were rerun. New component-removal controls and VRAM measurements extend evaluation. Existing splits, Table 6 training settings, and sampling-step counts are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix H.5/Table 16 separately removes FiLM, softmax, and gated residual connections, and jointly removes FiLM and softmax, while retaining dual attention and RRWP on ER-DAG and SBM. This substantially extends attribution of performance to individual architectural components. The DirLap comparison and expanded resource profiling provide additional supplementary evidence; earlier scalability and sampling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations across five sampling runs, one TPU Tiles run per tuning configuration, and three runs for conditional generation. Additional ablation rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice. No increased run count, new seed disclosure, confidence interval, or statistical-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Supporting results are substantially expanded and revised. New Table 16 reports ER-DAG V.U.N. of 4% without FiLM versus 94% for the full model. Table 14 adds DirLap results and revises SBM RRWP V.U.N. from 87.0±5.1 to 99.5±1.0, changing its ranking against MagLap variants. Tables 2 and 12 also revise SBM scores, while Table 8 adds and revises resource measurements. Table 1 and conditional-generation results remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain whether revised values reflect reruns or corrections.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a formal DirLap definition, Equation 31, with its Perron-vector construction and claimed spectral properties. Existing attention, DFM, and diffusion derivations remain unchanged. The new formula lacks a transpose in its second transition-matrix term, so its accompanying real-spectrum claim is not generally supported as printed.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions are retained. The introduction now explicitly scopes the model to small-to-medium graphs, up to approximately 200 nodes on average, and adds a comparative efficiency claim against diffusion-based alternatives.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds an explanation attributing DirLap's limitations to its inability to encode phase information, and H.5 interprets the new component ablations. Section 7 adds potential transfer to link prediction and node classification. Existing limitations concerning scalability, conditioning, and structural constraints are retained.

D1.justification: Table 8 provides broader model-specific training/sampling times, explicit MagLap Q variants, and newly reported VRAM usage. The anonymous code pointer is replaced by a named GitHub repository, and a reproducibility statement describes available scripts. Hardware, core implementation details, and most hyperparameters were already documented in v2.

R1.justification: The introduction adds efficiency positioning against diffusion methods, while Appendix B contrasts Chung's directed Laplacian with phase-based encodings. The related-work survey otherwise remains stable. Austin 2021a and 2021b duplicate a previously cited work rather than introduce a distinct study.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify directed edge categories, denoising predictions, and their connection to transition rates. v3 adds acknowledgements, reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements, updates the publication header, and inserts H.5. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer feature and update details; Figure 3 adds DirLap and revises plots and axes. Table 7 changes to grouped dataset columns, Table 8 gains model rows and VRAM, and Table 16 is new. Other figures, including the appendix graph visualizations, are retained with layout shifts.

improvement.justification: The new component controls in Table 16 and broader resource accounting in Table 8 improve assessment of architectural choices and computational tradeoffs relative to v2. Clearer explanations and the updated code pointer also help. These gains are limited by inconsistent propagation of revised SBM results—H.3 still states 87% where Table 12 reports 99.5%—and the transpose issue in the new DirLap equation. Overall, the added empirical support and transparency provide a modest net improvement.
